AIID-713.title: Purported Deepfake Video Falsely Depicts Biden Announcing National Draft for Ukraine
AIID-713.summary: A deepfake video featuring a synthetic version of President Joe Biden announcing a national military draft was circulated on social media. Although the creator later admitted the video was AI-generated, the initial post lacked this disclosure, leading to widespread public misinformation. Fact-checkers debunked the video, confirming it was a fabricated attempt to simulate a potential future scenario.

AIID-714.title: Microsoft-Powered New York City Chatbot Advises Illegal Practices
AIID-714.summary: New York City launched a Microsoft-powered AI chatbot as part of its 'MyCity' project to assist business owners with regulations and compliance. Investigations by The Markup and other outlets revealed that the bot frequently provided inaccurate and illegal advice, including incorrect information regarding housing discrimination, worker tip laws, and cash-payment mandates. The city has acknowledged the issues, characterizing the tool as a pilot program that requires ongoing improvement.
AIID-714.description: New York City's chatbot, launched under Mayor Eric Adams's plan to assist businesses, has been reportedly providing dangerously inaccurate legal advice. The Microsoft-powered bot allegedly informed users that landlords can refuse Section 8 vouchers and that businesses can operate cash-free, among other falsehoods. The city acknowledges the chatbot is a pilot program and commits to improvements while the errors are addressed.

AIID-715.title: Over 400 Purportedly AI-Driven Scams Reportedly Led to $8M Loss for Australians in 2023
AIID-715.summary: In 2023, Australian consumers lost over $8 million to investment scams that utilized AI-generated deepfake videos and fake news articles to impersonate celebrities. The National Anti-Scam Centre received over 400 reports of these incidents, which involved fraudulent trading platforms such as Quantum AI and Immediate Edge. Victims were lured into providing personal details or investing cryptocurrency, often resulting in total financial loss or persistent harassment.
AIID-715.description: In 2023, Australians reportedly lost over $8 million to scams involving purported deepfake videos and fake news articles that falsely endorsed investment trading platforms. The National Anti-Scam Centre received over 400 reports of these incidents. One man is reported to have lost over $80,000 in cryptocurrency.

AIID-716.title: Algorithmic Staffing Failures Linked to Resident Deaths at Leading Assisted-Living Chain Brookdale
AIID-716.summary: Brookdale Senior Living implemented an algorithm called 'Service Alignment' to determine staffing levels at its assisted-living facilities based on stopwatch-timed task efficiency. Former employees and court records allege the system failed to account for the complex, variable needs of elderly residents, resulting in chronic understaffing. This systemic understaffing has been linked to multiple instances of medical neglect, resident injuries, and deaths, including a fatal fall at a Jacksonville facility in 2021.
AIID-716.description: Brookdale Senior Living's algorithm-based staffing system, "Service Alignment," reportedly left facilities understaffed, leading to critical incidents. For example, on April 21, 2021, Louise Walker, a resident at Brookdale's Jacksonville facility, died after falling and being left unattended for over two hours. State investigators cited Brookdale for medical neglect. The algorithm has been linked to multiple incidents of neglect, injuries, and deaths, prompting lawsuits.

AIID-718.title: OpenAI, Google, and Meta Alleged to Have Overstepped Legal Boundaries for Training AI
AIID-718.summary: Major AI developers including OpenAI, Google, and Meta are reported to have engaged in aggressive data collection practices to train their models, potentially violating copyright laws and platform terms of service. These practices included transcribing YouTube videos without authorization and discussing the acquisition of publishing houses to secure training data. The report highlights the industry's desperate race for high-quality data to advance large language models.
AIID-718.description: In late 2021, OpenAI and other tech giants like Google and Meta reportedly faced data shortages for training AI models. OpenAI is said to have developed a tool called Whisper to transcribe over one million hours of YouTube videos, potentially violating YouTube’s terms of service. Similarly, Google allegedly transcribed YouTube videos, risking copyright infringements. Meta reportedly explored summarizing copyrighted texts without permission and debated acquiring Simon & Schuster for data.

AIID-719.title: Grok AI on X Created and Promoted False Iran Missile Strike News
AIID-719.summary: On April 4, 2024, X's AI chatbot Grok generated a false headline claiming that Iran had attacked Tel Aviv. This misinformation was automatically packaged and promoted by X's 'Explore' feature as a trending news story. The incident occurred because the AI relied on spam from verified accounts to generate its summary, demonstrating the risks of using automated AI for news curation without human oversight.
AIID-719.description: On April 4, 2024, X's AI chatbot Grok generated a false headline claiming "Iran Strikes Tel Aviv with Heavy Missiles," which was then promoted on X's trending news section. This misinformation, fueled by user spamming of fake news, falsely indicated a serious international conflict. The incident highlighted significant risks associated with relying on AI for content curation and demonstrated the potential for widespread dissemination of harmful misinformation.

These entities allegedly submit assignments containing hallucinations, such as descriptions of non-existent artworks and incorrect terminology, while showing minimal engagement with the college portal. The professor believes these bots are enrolled to fraudulently collect financial aid.

The professor reportedly believed the spambot students aimed to fraudulently obtain financial aid by remaining enrolled in courses.

AIID-722.title: Catholic AI Chatbot 'Father Justin' Claimed to Be a Real Priest, Prompting Retraction
AIID-722.summary: Catholic Answers released an AI chatbot named 'Father Justin' that was configured to impersonate a Catholic priest. The bot misled users by claiming to be ordained, offering sacraments, and providing controversial theological advice. Following public criticism, the organization rebranded the bot as a 'lay theologian' and removed its clerical attire.
AIID-722.description: Catholic advocacy group Catholic Answers released an AI priest called "Father Justin," which misleadingly claimed to be a real clergy member, offered sacraments, and provided controversial advice. After receiving criticism, the group rebranded the chatbot as a lay theologian to correct the misrepresentation. The incident is an instructive case with respect to deploying AI in sensitive contexts and the potential for causing confusion and harm.

AIID-726.title: A Self-Driving Cruise Robot Taxi Reportedly Struck and Dragged a Pedestrian 20 Feet
AIID-726.summary: In October 2023, a Cruise autonomous robotaxi in San Francisco dragged a pedestrian 20 feet after she had been struck by a separate human-driven vehicle. The Cruise vehicle, which had come to a stop on top of the victim, attempted to pull over while she was still trapped underneath. The incident resulted in severe injuries, a multi-million dollar settlement, the suspension of Cruise's driverless permits, and federal investigations into the company's safety disclosures and autonomous systems.
AIID-726.description: Cruise has settled for between $8 million and $12 million with a pedestrian dragged by one of its autonomous vehicles in October 2023. The incident, where the pedestrian was initially hit by a human-driven car and then dragged 20 feet by the Cruise vehicle, led to the suspension of Cruise's operations and increased regulatory scrutiny.

U.S. intelligence confirmed the voice was AI-generated, highlighting the use of synthetic media as a tool for foreign influence operations intended to erode trust in democratic institutions.

The incident involved the group Storm-1516, individuals linked to Valery Korovin, and potential veterans of the Internet Research Agency.

AIID-729.title: GPT-4o's Chinese Tokens Reportedly Compromised by Spam and Pornography Due to Inadequate Filtering
AIID-729.summary: Researchers discovered that the tokenizer for OpenAI's GPT-4o contains a disproportionate number of spam and pornographic tokens in Chinese, likely due to insufficient data cleaning during training. These 'polluted' tokens can be exploited to cause the model to hallucinate or bypass safety guardrails. Experts note that this vulnerability highlights a mismatch between the tokenizer's training data and the model's safety filters.
AIID-729.description: OpenAI's GPT-4o was found to have its Chinese token training data compromised by spam and pornographic phrases due to inadequate data cleaning. Tianle Cai, a Ph.D. student at Princeton University, identified that most of the longest Chinese tokens were irrelevant and inappropriate, primarily originating from spam and pornography websites. The polluted tokens could lead to hallucinations, poor performance, and potential misuse, undermining the chatbot's reliability and safety measures.

AIID-730.title: AI Deepfakes for Voter Outreach Flood Indian Elections
AIID-730.summary: During the 2024 Indian general elections, political parties and consultants have deployed AI-generated voice clones and video avatars to conduct personalized voter outreach at scale. These campaigns often lack disclosure, leading voters to believe they are interacting with real candidates. While proponents argue this improves engagement, critics highlight the risks of deception, lack of consent, and the potential for misinformation in a democratic process.
AIID-730.description: During the 2024 Indian elections, politicians used AI-generated deepfakes to reach voters, who might be unaware they're interacting with digital clones. This practice, used by various political parties, is not truthful, as voters may be misled by AI-generated content posing as genuine interactions with political figures.

AIID-731.title: Purportedly Hallucinated Software Packages with Potential Malware Reportedly Downloaded Thousands of Times by Developers
AIID-731.summary: Security researchers have identified a supply chain attack vector dubbed 'slopsquatting,' where AI coding assistants hallucinate non-existent software package names. Attackers monitor these hallucinations, register the fake packages with malicious payloads on public repositories like PyPI and npm, and wait for developers to install them based on AI suggestions. This vulnerability has already resulted in real-world codebases, such as Alibaba's GraphTranslator, incorporating malicious dependencies.
AIID-731.description: Large language models have reportedly hallucinated non-existent software package names, some of which were subsequently uploaded to public repositories and incorporated into real codebases. In one case, a package named huggingface-cli, which was purported to have been originally suggested by an AI model, was downloaded more than 15,000 times. This dynamic enables what security researchers have termed "slopsquatting," in which attackers register hallucinated package names and introduce potential malware into software supply chains.
AIID-731.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"2.2 AI system security vulnerabilities and attacks","justification":"The hallucinated packages create a security vulnerability in the software supply chain that can be exploited by malicious actors to distribute malware."},{"code":"4.3 Fraud, scams, and targeted manipulation","justification":"Attackers can weaponize these hallucinations to conduct scams or distribute malware, and some have already used AI to generate realistic-sounding fake package names at scale."}]
AIID-731.domainJustification: The incident is primarily caused by the AI systems' lack of capability and robustness, specifically their tendency to hallucinate non-existent software package names when generating code.
AIID-731.allegedDeployer: Developers using AI-generated suggestions, Bar Lanyado
AIID-731.allegedDeveloper: OpenAI, Meta, Google, DeepSeek AI, Cohere, BigScience
AIID-731.allegedHarmedParties: Users downstream of software contaminated by hallucinated packages, Trust in open-source repositories and AI-assisted coding tools, Software ecosystems, Organizations that incorporated fake dependencies, Developers and businesses incorporating AI-suggested packages, Alibaba
AIID-731.aiGoalJustification: The AI models were primarily used as coding assistants to generate software code and package recommendations based on user prompts.

AIID-732.title: Whisper Speech-to-Text AI Reportedly Found to Create Violent Hallucinations
AIID-732.summary: Researchers at Cornell University discovered that OpenAI's Whisper speech-to-text system frequently hallucinates violent language, fake websites, and fabricated personal information when processing audio containing long pauses. These hallucinations disproportionately affect individuals with speech impairments, such as those with aphasia. The study highlights significant risks for downstream applications in sensitive fields like legal, medical, and hiring processes.
AIID-732.description: Researchers at Cornell reportedly found that OpenAI's Whisper, a speech-to-text system, can hallucinate violent language and fabricated details, especially with long pauses in speech, such as from those with speech impairments. Analyzing 13,000 clips, they determined 1% contained harmful hallucinations. These errors pose risks in hiring, legal trials, and medical documentation. The study suggests improving model training to reduce these hallucinations for diverse speaking patterns.

AIID-732.domainJustification: Whisper performs unequally across groups because it is significantly more likely to hallucinate and produce errors when transcribing speech from individuals with speech impairments due to their longer pauses.

AIID-733.title: Auto Insurers Allegedly Are Surreptitiously Collecting and Scoring Driver Data
AIID-733.summary: The insurance industry is increasingly utilizing AI-powered telematics to track and score individual driving behaviors via smartphone apps and vehicle data. These scores, generated by companies like Arity, are used to influence insurance premiums, often through opaque consent processes that leave consumers unaware of the extent of the surveillance. This practice raises significant privacy concerns and risks of discriminatory pricing based on driving habits or socioeconomic status.
AIID-733.description: The insurance industry allegedly uses AI and telematics to score drivers based on behaviors tracked by automakers and apps like Life360. Data, often collected without clear consent, may affect insurance rates and raises privacy concerns. Consumers are largely unaware of this surveillance, leading to potential misuse and discrimination based on driving habits or socioeconomic factors.

AIID-734.title: Leading AI Models Reportedly Found to Mimic Russian Disinformation in 33% of Cases and to Cite Fake Moscow News Sites
AIID-734.summary: A NewsGuard audit of 10 leading AI chatbots found that they repeated Russian disinformation narratives in approximately 32% of responses. The models frequently cited fake local news sites as reliable sources, authoritatively presenting false claims as fact. This behavior demonstrates how AI can inadvertently validate and amplify disinformation campaigns, posing risks to public information integrity during election cycles.
AIID-734.description: An audit by NewsGuard revealed that leading chatbots, including ChatGPT-4, You.com’s Smart Assistant, and others, repeated Russian disinformation narratives in one-third of their responses. These narratives originated from a network of fake news sites created by John Mark Dougan (Incident 701). The audit tested 570 prompts across 10 AI chatbots, showing that AI remains a tool for spreading disinformation despite efforts to prevent misuse.

AIID-736.title: Underground Market for LLMs Powers Malware and Phishing Scams
AIID-736.summary: Researchers from Indiana University identified a widespread underground ecosystem where malicious actors use various LLMs to facilitate cybercrime. These 'Mallas' (malicious services) leverage both proprietary models like GPT-4 and open-source models to generate malware, phishing content, and scam websites. The study highlights the prevalence of jailbreaking techniques and the use of uncensored models to bypass safety guardrails.
AIID-736.description: A study by Indiana University researchers uncovered widespread misuse of large language models (LLMs) for cybercrime. Cybercriminals, according to that study, use LLMs like OpenAI's GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 to create malware, phishing scams, and scam websites. These models are available on underground markets, often bypassing safety checks through jailbreaking. Named malicious LLMs are BadGPT, XXXGPT, Evil-GPT, WormGPT, FraudGPT, BLACKHATGPT, EscapeGPT, DarkGPT, and WolfGPT.

AIID-737.title: Amandine Le Pen Deepfake Account Misleads Thousands on TikTok
AIID-737.summary: Multiple TikTok accounts using AI deepfake technology have been created to impersonate fictional nieces of French politician Marine Le Pen. These accounts, which have amassed tens of thousands of followers, promote far-right political parties and have been used to solicit donations from users. The incident has raised significant concerns regarding political manipulation, the spread of misinformation ahead of EU elections, and the violation of personality rights through the unauthorized use of likenesses.
AIID-737.description: A TikTok account, "Amandine Le Pen," created using AI deepfake technology, impersonated a fictional niece of Marine Le Pen, amassing over 30,000 followers. The account spread pro-RN messages and solicited donations, misleading users and exploiting political influence. Visual inconsistencies revealed the deepfake, raising concerns about AI misuse for political manipulation, identity theft, and violation of personal rights, especially with similar accounts proliferating, such as "Lena Maréchal Lepen."

AIID-738.title: Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) Algorithm Wrongly Flags 200,000 for Housing Benefit Fraud
AIID-738.summary: A government-deployed automated system used by the UK's Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) to flag housing benefit claims for fraud investigation significantly underperformed, incorrectly identifying over 200,000 legitimate claims as high risk. This resulted in unnecessary investigations, significant stress for claimants, and the waste of approximately £4.4 million in public funds. The incident has raised concerns regarding algorithmic bias, lack of transparency, and the potential for discriminatory impacts on vulnerable populations.
AIID-738.description: A Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) algorithm wrongly flagged over 200,000 UK housing benefit claims as high risk, resulting in unnecessary investigations. Two-thirds of these flagged claims were legitimate, causing wasted public funds and stress for claimants. Despite initial success in a pilot, the algorithm's real-world performance fell short. This incident highlights the risks of overreliance on automated systems in welfare administration.

AIID-739.title: Scammers Allegedly Use Deepfake of Hong Kong Entertainer Andy Lau to Steal NT$2.64 Million from Fan
AIID-739.summary: A 62-year-old woman in New Taipei City was defrauded of NT$2.64 million by scammers who used AI face-changing and voice-cloning technology to impersonate a Hong Kong entertainer during video calls. The victim, a long-time fan, was convinced to wire money for a purported visit to Taiwan. Police intervened after the victim's family became suspicious, leading to the arrest of a woman who had been recruited by the same scam group to collect cash.
AIID-739.description: Scammers allegedly defrauded a woman in New Taipei City of NT$2.64 million (US$81,116) by impersonating Hong Kong entertainer Andy Lau using purported deepfakes. The alleged scam convinced the victim, a long-time fan, through a video call that "Lau" needed funds for a visit to Taiwan. The victim reportedly wired the money, but her family suspected a scam and involved the police. An alleged scammer was arrested after attempting to collect a staged cash payment.

AIID-740.title: Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) AI Systems Allegedly Discriminate Against Single Mothers
AIID-740.summary: Researchers and FOI requests indicate that the UK's Universal Credit system, which uses automated processes for eligibility and fraud detection, disproportionately impacts single mothers. The system's algorithms reportedly suffer from biases encoded through historical data and fail to account for payment frequency, leading to significant income volatility and financial hardship for claimants.
AIID-740.description: Researchers have argued that the Department for Work and Pensions' Universal Credit system disproportionately impacts single mothers. Automated processes in the system, designed to determine eligibility and detect fraud, are reported to have introduced biases, leading to financial instability and hardship. The algorithms allegedly miscalculate earnings and delay childcare reimbursements, in turn exacerbating income volatility and debt among single mothers.

AIID-742.title: Grok AI Model Reportedly Fails to Produce Reliable News in Wake of Trump Assassination Attempt
AIID-742.summary: During the aftermath of the attempted assassination of Donald Trump, the AI model Grok, used by X for automated news aggregation, generated and promoted false headlines. These included incorrect claims that Vice President Kamala Harris had been shot and misidentification of the shooter, stemming from the model's failure to distinguish between factual news and sarcastic or speculative social media posts. The incident highlights the risks of using AI to automate real-time news delivery without human oversight.

These errors show the pitfalls of relying on AI for real-time news aggregation, as it allegedly amplified unverified claims and failed to recognize sarcasm, undermining its reliability.

AIID-743.title: Gemini AI Allegedly Reads Google Drive Files Without Explicit User Consent

AIID-747.title: Fatalities Reportedly Occur Despite VioGén Algorithm's Low or Negligible Risk Scores
AIID-747.summary: The VioGén algorithm, used by Spanish police to assess domestic violence risk, has been linked to fatal outcomes for victims who were incorrectly classified as low or negligible risk. Despite its intended purpose of prioritizing resources for vulnerable individuals, the system's reliance on potentially flawed input data and its influence on human decision-making have resulted in cases where victims received insufficient protection and were subsequently killed by their abusers. Government figures and independent reviews indicate that a significant number of homicide victims had been previously assessed by the system as low risk.
AIID-747.description: The VioGén algorithm was designed to help Spanish police assess and prioritize the risk of repeat domestic violence incidents. However, its low-risk assessment of Lobna Hemid reportedly led to inadequate protection; her husband murdered her. Since 2007, 247 women have been killed after being assessed by VioGén. A review of 98 homicides found that 55 of the slain women were scored as negligible or low risk.

The incident created unnecessary labor for both the user and PayPal's human support, demonstrating the potential harm of deploying generative AI without thorough testing and error handling mechanisms.

AIID-749.title: Hoodline Accused of Misleadingly Attributing AI-Generated Articles to Human Authors
AIID-749.summary: The news outlet Hoodline was found to be publishing AI-generated articles under fake human bylines, complete with fabricated biographies and AI-generated headshots. AIID-750.title: AI Chatbots Reportedly Inaccurately Conveyed Real-Time Political News
AIID-750.summary: During a period of significant breaking political news, including the Trump rally shooting and President Biden's campaign withdrawal, multiple popular AI chatbots failed to provide accurate, real-time information. Testing revealed that these systems often provided outdated, incorrect, or evasive responses, highlighting their limitations in handling fast-paced news cycles. While some companies implemented guardrails to redirect political queries, the overall performance raised concerns about the reliability of AI as a source for current events.
AIID-750.description: Over a week of back-to-back, significant breaking political news stories, including the Trump rally shooting and Biden’s campaign withdrawal, AI chatbots reportedly failed to provide accurate real-time updates. These incidents suggest the continuing need for improved AI capabilities and caution in their deployment for real-time news dissemination.

AIID-753.summary: BNN Breaking, a news outlet, utilized generative AI to mass-produce low-quality, often fabricated news stories to drive advertising revenue. AIID-755.title: Purported Deepfake Targets Olena Zelenska in Alleged Russian Disinformation Campaign

AIID-760.title: False Election Data on Kamala Harris Reportedly Circulated via Grok AI Chatbot
AIID-760.summary: Following President Biden's withdrawal from the 2024 presidential race, the AI chatbot Grok on X generated false information claiming that Vice President Kamala Harris had missed ballot deadlines in nine U.S. states. This misinformation was widely shared on social media, prompting five secretaries of state to send an open letter to Elon Musk demanding immediate corrections and the implementation of reliable election information sources. The false information persisted for over a week before being corrected.
AIID-760.description: After President Joe Biden stepped aside as a presidential candidate on July 21, 2024, the AI chatbot Grok on X reportedly falsely informed users that Vice President Kamala Harris missed the ballot deadline in nine states. AIID-761.title: TikTok AI System Used to Amplify Election Disinformation by Foreign Networks
AIID-761.summary: A Wall Street Journal investigation identified 91 accounts across TikTok, linked to foreign networks in China, Nigeria, Iran, and Vietnam, that used AI-generated content to spread political misinformation regarding the 2024 U.S. presidential election. These accounts exploited TikTok's recommendation algorithm to achieve high engagement, with some operations appearing to be motivated by financial gain through creator rewards programs. The incident highlights the ongoing challenge social media platforms face in moderating AI-generated disinformation at scale.
AIID-761.description: AI-generated misinformation on TikTok, driven by foreign networks, has flooded the platform with false narratives about the 2024 U.S. presidential election. Thousands of videos spreading political lies were identified, potentially influencing millions of users. AIID-762.title: Grok AI Reportedly Generates Offensive and Violent Images Without Proper Safeguards
AIID-762.summary: xAI's Grok-2 image generation tool was released on the X platform with minimal safety guardrails, allowing users to generate offensive, violent, and sexually explicit deepfakes of public figures and copyrighted characters. The lack of content moderation and absence of watermarking on generated images raised significant concerns regarding misinformation, harassment, and copyright infringement. While some users and the company defended the tool's lack of restrictions as a commitment to free speech and innovation, experts and legal professionals highlighted the potential for severe legal and ethical liabilities.
AIID-762.description: Elon Musk’s Grok AI, launched on X, generated offensive and violent images without adequate safety controls. The AI produced deepfakes of public figures like Taylor Swift, Kamala Harris, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, as well as copyrighted characters such as Mickey Mouse in inappropriate scenarios. Despite claiming adherence to certain content guidelines, Grok's outputs included politically charged and explicit imagery

AIID-770.title: Microsoft Copilot Falsely Accuses Journalist Martin Bernklau of Crimes
AIID-770.summary: Microsoft Copilot repeatedly generated defamatory content falsely identifying a German court reporter as a perpetrator of crimes he had covered in his professional capacity. Despite attempts to have the information removed, the false claims persisted, highlighting the unreliability of LLMs as research tools and the challenges of enforcing data accuracy and privacy rights under GDPR.
AIID-770.description: Microsoft's Copilot is reported to have falsely accused veteran court reporter Martin Bernklau of committing serious crimes, including child abuse and fraud. Attempts by Microsoft to remove the false entries were only temporarily successful, as the defamatory information reportedly reappeared.

AIID-773.title: Chatbot in Workplace Training at Bunbury Prison Reveals Real Names in Sexual Harassment Case
AIID-773.summary: During a workplace training session at Bunbury Prison, a trainer used Microsoft's Copilot to generate case study scenarios. The AI produced a scenario that included the real name of a former employee involved in an active sexual harassment case, despite claiming the scenario was fictional. This incident highlights the risks of AI 'regurgitation' of sensitive, publicly available information when used for content generation.
AIID-773.description: During workplace training at Bunbury Prison in Western Australia, a trainer used Microsoft's Copilot AI chatbot to generate case study scenarios. The chatbot produced a scenario that included the real name of a former employee involved in a sexual harassment case, revealing sensitive information.
AIID-773.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"3.1 False or misleading information","justification":"The AI system explicitly generated false meta-information by claiming 'this case study is entirely fictional' when it actually contained real names and active court details, misleading the user."},{"code":"1.2 Exposure to toxic content","justification":"The AI system exposed users in a workplace training environment to sensitive, triggering, and inappropriate real-world sexual harassment details involving their former colleague."}]
AIID-773.domainJustification: The AI system failed to perform reliably by failing to adhere to the negative constraint of generating a fictional scenario, instead regurgitating real-world sensitive data and falsely labeling it as fictional.

AIID-776.title: Megalopolis Trailer Included Fake AI-Generated Quotes Attributed to Film Critics
AIID-776.summary: Lionsgate recalled a trailer for the film 'Megalopolis' after it was discovered to contain fabricated, AI-generated quotes attributed to prominent film critics. AIID-777.title: South Korea Experiences a Surge of Explicit Deepfake Pornography
AIID-777.summary: In August 2024, South Korea experienced a massive surge in non-consensual sexually explicit deepfake imagery targeting women and minors. Perpetrators, often teenagers, used AI tools to manipulate social media photos of classmates, teachers, and neighbors into pornographic content, distributing them through Telegram chat groups. The incident has caused widespread panic, leading many women to delete their social media presence, and has prompted government investigations and calls for stricter regulation of both AI tools and messaging platforms.
AIID-777.description: At the end of August 2024, South Korean authorities began investigating a significant surge in the creation and dissemination, often via Telegram, of explicit deepfake pornography created without consent from the stolen social media content of female classmates, teachers, and neighbors.

AIID-778.summary: Amazon's Alexa voice assistant generated politically biased responses regarding the 2024 US presidential candidates, appearing to endorse Kamala Harris while refusing to provide reasons to vote for Donald Trump. AIID-786.title: Fraudsters Use Deepfake Video of Tim Cook to Promote Apple Crypto Scam on YouTube
AIID-786.summary: Fraudsters exploited the timing of Apple's iPhone 14 announcement to host fake YouTube live streams. These streams used repurposed, edited footage of tech CEOs like Tim Cook and Elon Musk to deceive viewers into visiting fraudulent cryptocurrency websites. The streams reached tens of thousands of viewers before being removed by YouTube for violating terms of service.

AIID-787.title: Deepfake ID Sales Allegedly Persist as OnlyFake Reportedly Relaunches with New Fraud Tools
AIID-787.summary: OnlyFake was an AI-powered platform that generated and sold over 10,000 counterfeit identity documents, including passports and driver's licenses, to facilitate fraud. The service allowed users to bypass Know Your Customer (KYC) verification protocols on major cryptocurrency exchanges and financial institutions. The operator, Yurii Nazarenko, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit fraud, acknowledging that the platform earned hundreds of thousands of dollars and enabled money laundering.
AIID-787.description: Researchers from Au10tix discovered the relaunch of OnlyFake, a site offering AI-generated fake IDs. Despite an earlier takedown, the site reemerged with disclaimers and new tools, including handwritten signature generation. These fakes are challenging biometric verification systems and are reportedly being used to perpetuate fraudulent activity.

AIID-787.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of the OnlyFake platform was to generate highly realistic, synthetic images of counterfeit identity documents to deceive verification systems.

AIID-788.title: Instagram's Algorithm Reportedly Recommended Sexual Content to Teenagers' Accounts
AIID-788.summary: Investigations by The Wall Street Journal and a researcher revealed that Instagram's AI-driven Reels algorithm consistently recommended sexually suggestive and explicit content to test accounts registered as 13-year-olds. Despite Meta's public commitments to restrict such material for minors, the system served adult-oriented content, including promotions for sex workers, within minutes of account creation. Internal company documents indicate that Meta has been aware of these issues for years, with data showing minors were disproportionately exposed to prohibited content compared to adult users.
AIID-788.description: Tests by The Wall Street Journal and a researcher reportedly revealed that Instagram's AI-driven Reels algorithm recommends sexually suggestive content to accounts listed as 13 years old. AIID-789.title: Independent News Sites Flagged as Spam by Facebook's AI Moderation System
AIID-789.summary: Facebook's AI moderation system has been incorrectly flagging and removing legitimate news articles from independent publishers as spam. This issue has affected publishers across the UK, US, and Europe, causing significant disruption to content distribution and website traffic. Publishers have reported difficulty in contacting Meta to resolve these erroneous removals, which have impacted their ability to reach audiences during critical periods like general elections.
AIID-789.description: Facebook's AI moderation system mistakenly flagged and removed legitimate news articles from independent local publishers as spam. This affected publishers worldwide, disrupting content distribution and impacting traffic. Despite attempts to appeal, many publishers received no response.

AIID-791.title: Google AI Error Prompts Parents to Use Fecal Matter in Child Training Exercise
AIID-791.summary: Google's AI Overview feature generated harmful and unsanitary advice for parents by misinterpreting a potty training technique. The AI failed to understand that a source video used the term 'poo' to refer to shaving cream, leading the system to explicitly recommend that parents use actual human feces. Google acknowledged the error, attributing it to a failure in contextual interpretation.
AIID-791.description: Google's AI Overview feature mistakenly advised parents to use human feces in a potty training exercise, misinterpreting a method that uses shaving cream or peanut butter as a substitute. This incident is another example of an AI failure in grasping contextual nuances that can lead to potentially harmful, and in this case unsanitary, recommendations. Google has acknowledged the error.

AIID-793.title: AllHere's Chatbot 'Ed' Fails and Costs Los Angeles Unified School District $6 Million
AIID-793.summary: The AI education startup AllHere, which developed a chatbot named Ed for the Los Angeles Unified School District, collapsed following the discovery of a multi-million dollar fraud scheme orchestrated by its founder, Joanna Smith-Griffin. The company misrepresented its revenue, customer base, and financial health to investors while securing contracts with school districts. The project was abruptly terminated in June 2024, leaving school districts without promised technical support and resulting in federal criminal charges against the founder.
AIID-793.description: The Los Angeles Unified School District invested up to $6 million in developing the AI chatbot "Ed," meant to provide academic and mental health support for students. The chatbot allegedly failed to meet expectations, and the project collapsed when AllHere, the contracted start-up, faced financial difficulties. Prince George's County Public Schools in Maryland was also affected. Founder Joanna Smith-Griffin was removed as CEO in June 2024 and later arrested on fraud charges.

AIID-796.title: Facebook's Content Moderation System Flagged and Removed Emergency Updates as Spam During Wildfires
AIID-796.summary: Facebook's AI-driven content moderation system incorrectly flagged and removed numerous posts containing critical emergency information during California's wildfire season. The system categorized posts from official sources and volunteer responders as spam, preventing the dissemination of vital evacuation and fire-tracking updates. The issue persisted for months, with users receiving no notifications when their posts were removed, leading to concerns about life-threatening delays in information access.
AIID-796.description: Facebook's AI moderation system wrongly flagged and removed dozens of posts containing vital emergency information during California's wildfire season, including real-time updates on evacuations and fire tracking. Posts from official sources like Cal Fire and the U.S. Forest Service were marked as spam, potentially endangering lives by restricting access to crucial updates. Despite user complaints, the issue persisted, with Facebook acknowledging the problem only after media inquiry.

AIID-801.title: Bias in AI Deepfake Detection Undermines Election Security in Global South
AIID-801.summary: AI deepfake detection tools are exhibiting significant performance biases, as they are primarily trained on Western-centric data. This results in high error rates when analyzing content from the Global South, including false positives for non-native English speakers and failures to recognize lower-quality media common in those regions. These inaccuracies undermine election integrity and hinder the ability of journalists and researchers to combat misinformation effectively.
AIID-801.description: AI deepfake detection tools are reportedly failing voters in the Global South due to biases in their training data. These tools, which prioritize English language and Western faces, show reduced accuracy when detecting manipulated content from non-Western regions. As a result of this detection gap, election integrity faces threats from and the amplification of misinformation, which leaves journalists and researchers with inadequate resources to combat the issue.

AIID-802.title: Purported Deepfake of Brian May Allegedly Exploited in Scam Offering Fake Queen Backstage Tickets

The real Brian May publicly denounced the scam as a 'vile' criminal attempt to steal money from fans. AIID-804.title: AI-Generated Fake 'True Crime' Video About Non-Existent Littleton Murder Goes Viral
AIID-804.summary: A YouTube channel named 'True Crime Case Files' has been using generative AI to produce and distribute hundreds of entirely fabricated 'true crime' documentaries. These videos, which feature AI-generated narration and imagery, have garnered millions of views and deceived viewers into believing in non-existent murders and criminal cases. Law enforcement officials and experts warn that this content not only scams viewers for profit but also threatens to undermine public trust in the judicial system and the credibility of real-world evidence.
AIID-804.description: An AI-generated "true crime" video on YouTube falsely depicted a Littleton man's "secret gay love affair" and murder by his stepson. The 25-minute video, which garnered nearly 2 million views, fabricated details and used deepfake technology to deceive viewers into believing the story was real. Despite being flagged as false by local authorities and lacking credible sources, the video sparked widespread misinformation and outrage online.

AIID-805.title: Senator Ben Cardin Reportedly Received a Purported Deepfake Zoom Call Impersonating Former Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba
AIID-805.summary: Senator Ben Cardin was targeted in a sophisticated deepfake operation where a malign actor impersonated former Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba during a Zoom call. The impersonator used AI-generated voice and video to attempt to bait the Senator into commenting on sensitive political and foreign policy issues, including the use of long-range missiles in Russia. The Senator grew suspicious, ended the call, and reported the incident to authorities, who confirmed the impersonation. The event has prompted security warnings to other lawmakers regarding the increasing use of AI in social engineering and election interference.

AIID-806.title: Criminal Group Uses AI Deepfake Technology to Steal Personal Data in Hangzhou, Zhejiang
AIID-806.summary: A criminal group in China utilized an AI multimodal model to perform 'face-swapping' attacks, bypassing facial recognition systems on major platforms. By converting static photos into dynamic videos, the group successfully breached user accounts to steal personal information, which was then sold to fraud syndicates. The Hangzhou Public Security Bureau investigated the case and arrested four suspects in August 2024, noting that the group had profited approximately 200,000 yuan from these activities.
AIID-806.description: A criminal group in China used AI face-swapping technology to bypass face recognition systems on major platforms, steal personal data, and sell it to fraud syndicates. The group generated convincing video simulations from static photos to breach accounts, reportedly earning 200,000 yuan. After an investigation by the Hangzhou Public Security Bureau, four suspects were arrested across the provinces of Anhui, Guizhou, and Zhejiang.

AIID-807.title: ChatGPT Reportedly Introduces Errors in Critical Child Protection Court Report
AIID-807.summary: A child protection worker in Victoria, Australia, used ChatGPT to draft a court-submitted Protection Application Report, inputting sensitive case details. The AI-generated content contained significant inaccuracies, including mischaracterizing evidence of sexual abuse as positive parenting behavior. This incident led to an investigation by the Office of the Victorian Information Commissioner (OVIC), which found that the department failed to protect sensitive information and issued a compliance notice requiring a ban on the use of generative AI tools by child protection staff.
AIID-807.description: A child protection worker in Victoria, Australia reportedly used ChatGPT to draft a report submitted to the Children's Court. The purportedly AI-generated report contained inaccuracies and downplayed risks to the child, allegedly resulting in a privacy breach when sensitive information was shared with OpenAI.

AIID-808.title: Infinite Campus AI-Driven Student Risk Model Leads to Cuts in Support for Nevada's Low-Income Schools
AIID-808.summary: Nevada implemented an AI system developed by Infinite Campus to identify at-risk students for funding purposes. The model significantly reduced the number of students classified as at-risk, leading to substantial budget cuts for schools serving low-income populations and raising concerns about transparency, algorithmic bias, and the adequacy of support for vulnerable students.
AIID-808.description: An AI system developed by Infinite Campus and deployed by Nevada to identify at-risk students led to a sharp reduction in the number classified as needing support, dropping from 270,000 to 65,000. The reclassification caused significant budget cuts in schools serving low-income populations. The drastic reduction in identified at-risk students reportedly left thousands of vulnerable children without resources and support.

AIID-809.title: TikTok Hosts AI-Generated English-Language Hitler Speeches with Millions of Views
AIID-809.summary: Media Matters reported that AI-generated English-language speeches of Adolf Hitler are proliferating on TikTok, accumulating millions of views. These clips often feature misleading translations and are used to glorify the Nazi leader and promote hateful ideologies, violating the platform's community guidelines. Despite some removals, dedicated accounts continue to circulate this content, and TikTok's search features have been observed facilitating user access to these materials.
AIID-809.description: AI-generated English-language Adolf Hitler speeches have been proliferating on TikTok. While some content has been removed, many accounts reportedly continue to post similar videos.

AIID-811.title: AI-Powered Transcription Services Allegedly Leak Confidential Workplace Discussions
AIID-811.summary: AI-powered transcription tools, specifically Otter.ai's OtterPilot, caused multiple privacy breaches by automatically recording and distributing transcripts of private meetings to unauthorized participants. In one instance, a VC firm's confidential post-meeting discussion was leaked to an external party, resulting in a cancelled deal. In a separate incident at a hospital, an unauthorized AI agent accessed a virtual meeting via a former employee's calendar, exposing the personal health information of seven patients to 65 recipients.
AIID-811.description: AI-powered meeting assistants, such as Otter.ai’s OtterPilot and Zoom's AI Companion, have reportedly shared sensitive and private conversations beyond the intended audience. These AI tools, which are set to automatically record and distribute meeting transcripts, allegedly sent confidential discussions after participants had left the meeting, the consequences of which led to unintended exposure of proprietary information, privacy breaches, and potential reputational harm.

AIID-811.causalJustification: The privacy leaks were directly caused by the AI transcription tool autonomously joining meetings, transcribing them, and automatically emailing summaries to unauthorized recipients without direct human intervention.
AIID-811.euAiActRiskReasoning: Limited Risk: The system is an AI-powered transcription and meeting assistant, which falls under Limited Risk (Level 3) as it requires transparency obligations such as notifying meeting participants when they are interacting with an AI recording tool.
AIID-811.reasonForConfidence: The reports provide highly detailed, consistent, and official accounts (including a formal letter from the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario) of the hospital breach, as well as first-hand accounts from Alex Bilzerian regarding the VC firm incident. The technical behavior of the AI tool (calendar integration, auto-joining, auto-sharing) is clearly explained.
AIID-811.ambiguitiesIdentified: None of significance; the settings and behaviors of Otter.ai that led to the leaks are well-documented.
AIID-811.alternativeInterpretations: One could argue the hospital breach was primarily a human offboarding failure rather than an AI failure, but the autonomous action of the AI agent in joining and emailing the transcript makes it a clear AI safety incident.
AIID-811.natSecSummary: Unintentional privacy leaks caused by Otter.ai's autonomous transcription agent resulted in the exposure of sensitive patient health data and confidential venture capital discussions. While demonstrating the risks of autonomous SaaS agents and shadow AI, the national security impact remains minor and localized, with no threats to critical infrastructure, sovereignty, or state-level intelligence.
AIID-811.natSecImminenceJustification: Represents an ongoing strategic concern regarding shadow AI usage and data governance rather than an active, imminent national security crisis.
AIID-811.natSecAutonomyJustification: The AI agent autonomously accessed, recorded, transcribed, and distributed meeting information based on calendar integration without real-time human intervention.
AIID-811.natSecNoveltyJustification: Represents an advancement of traditional data leak vectors, leveraging autonomous agentic features to bypass standard meeting access controls.
AIID-811.natSecPhysicalJustification: No threat to physical systems, infrastructure, or human safety was reported in connection with this incident.
AIID-811.natSecInformationJustification: The incident involved localized privacy breaches of commercial and patient data, with no indications of state-sponsored intelligence compromise or information warfare.
AIID-811.natSecSovereigntyJustification: No impact on government decision-making, state authority, or electoral systems.
AIID-811.natSecEconomicJustification: The incident caused localized economic harm, including a cancelled venture capital deal and administrative remediation costs for the affected hospital, but did not threaten national economic stability.
AIID-811.natSecSocietalJustification: The leak of personal health information of patients represents a localized violation of privacy rights, but did not scale to systemic human rights abuses or societal instability.

AIID-812.title: Deepfake Nudes Targeting Underage Female Students at Collège Béliveau in Winnipeg Shared Online
AIID-812.summary: In December 2023, female students at Collège Béliveau in Winnipeg were targeted by the creation and online distribution of non-consensual AI-generated nude images. The perpetrators reportedly used publicly accessible social media photos to generate the explicit content. The incident caused significant emotional distress among the student body and prompted an investigation by the Winnipeg Police Service, though no criminal charges were ultimately filed due to legal complexities surrounding AI-generated content.
AIID-812.description: At Collège Béliveau in Winnipeg, female students between grades 7-12 were targeted in the creation of deepfake nudes, which were then distributed online. Specific numbers and identities of victims and perpetrators were not released, and no charges were ultimately filed owing to the gap between existing laws and the nature of the incident.
